messages:
Maya: Quick heads up — Taleo (Head of ML) agreed to a case study. Interview scheduled Wed 10am PT. Need quote approval + legal sign-off. Outline: latency 3x improvement after Dedicated, cost ~45% lower (draft).
Chris: Nice. Can we get a one-line hero quote for the web header? Short, customer voice.
Lena: Will gather CS notes and confirm exact numbers with the customer. Also can get the dashboard screenshot.
Maya: Dropping draft transcript & assets: Recording -> `taleo-interview-2026-03-20.mp3`, Transcript -> https://drive.redwood/taleo/case-draft-transcript.txt
Alex: Sales: want to avoid ARR mentions without consent. If customer ok, we can include impact statement. @Maya please confirm before publishing.
Sam (Legal): I'll scan for PII and tricky claims. Please add the signed release to the thread when you have it.
Maya: Draft quote proposed: `Redwood Dedicated cut our inference costs by ~45% and made latency consistent.` CS/customer approval needed.
Lena: Customer prefers softer language — they suggested `up to 45%`. I'm pinging them now.
Jorge: For benchmark attribution, can we say `production inference workload (mixed batch, 99th p95)`? maybe simpler: `production workload, steady-state`.
Maya: Timeline: need marketing-ready copy by Fri EOD to slot into next week's newsletter.
Sam (Legal): Redlines: remove exact GPU counts and raw ARR; replace with 'in our production environment'. Also need attached signed release: `taleo_release_signed.pdf`
Chris: Adding to editorial tracker now.
PublishBot: uploaded: /marketing/case-studies/taleo/draft-v1.md (uploader: Maya)
Maya: @Lena can you confirm quote wording and secure customer sign-off? I'll send the release form now.
Lena: Pinged customer — they said they'll review by tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
Alex: Once signed, route webinar leads to `Alex_QBR` pipeline. I'll prep the lead form.
Maya: Thanks all — final rule: avoid absolutes, attribute numbers to 'customer tests'. I'll update the draft after the signed release is in.
